court: Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit

issues.label: Federal jurisdiction over Mrs. Smith post-Castro-Huerta
issues.why: Court must decide whether Castro-Huerta strips federal subject-matter jurisdiction over a non-Indian's crime against an Indian in Indian country.

issues.label: GCA/ACA basis for prosecuting non-Indian defendant
issues.why: Court must confirm the GCA and ACA properly supply the substantive offense and jurisdiction for Mrs. Smith.

issues.label: MCA jurisdiction over Mr. Smith
issues.why: Court must confirm the Major Crimes Act properly reaches the Indian defendant's child abuse and neglect offenses in Indian country.

issues.label: Indian country status of offense location
issues.why: Jurisdiction under both MCA and GCA depends on establishing the offenses occurred in Indian country.

issues.label: Indian status of defendant and victim
issues.why: Jurisdictional framework turns on Mr. Smith's Indian status, Mrs. Smith's non-Indian status, and the victim's Indian status.

issues.label: Aiding-and-abetting a non-Indian under MCA
issues.why: Court must decide whether the MCA can support charging non-Indian Mrs. Smith as an aider/abettor.

issues.label: Aiding-and-abetting an Indian under GCA
issues.why: Court must decide whether the GCA can support Mr. Smith's aiding/abetting given the Indian-against-Indian exception.

issues.label: Whether aiding-abetting requires independent jurisdictional basis
issues.why: Court must determine if 18 U.S.C. § 2 liability derives from each defendant's own jurisdictional statute or the principal's.

issues.label: Preservation and standard of review for instruction objection
issues.why: The timing and scope of the Smiths' objection affect whether de novo or plain-error review applies.

issues.label: Existence of analogous guideline for child abuse
issues.why: Court must determine whether a sufficiently analogous guideline (e.g., § 2A2.2) exists under § 2X5.1.

issues.label: Applicability of § 2X5.1 versus § 3553 only
issues.why: Court must decide whether the absence of an analogous guideline permits reliance solely on § 3553 factors.

issues.label: Correctness of § 2A2.2 aggravated-assault analogy
issues.why: Court must assess whether aggravated assault is sufficiently analogous to child abuse by injury.

issues.label: Procedural reasonableness of Mr. Smith's sentence
issues.why: A miscalculated Guidelines range would render the sentence procedurally unreasonable requiring resentencing.

issues.label: Substantive reasonableness of imposed sentences
issues.why: Court's application of § 3553(a) factors and the 180/240-month terms may require reasonableness review.

issues.label: Timeliness of Mrs. Smith's second Rule 29/33 motion
issues.why: Court must determine whether the amended post-trial motion was filed within the mandatory deadlines.

issues.label: Whether Rule 33/29 deadlines are jurisdictional or waivable
issues.why: The characterization affects whether untimeliness could be excused or forfeited by the government.

issues.label: Victim status of letter authors under § 3771(e)(2)
issues.why: Court must decide whether the letter writers qualify as crime victims entitled to submit impact statements.

issues.label: Adequacy of time to review victim-impact letters
issues.why: Court must assess whether denying more time to review 22-hour-late letters prejudiced the defendants.

issues.label: Reliance on improper sentencing information
issues.why: If the letters were improperly considered, the sentences may require vacatur or resentencing.

issues.label: Sufficiency of evidence for child abuse convictions
issues.why: Rule 29 requires assessing whether evidence supports each element of abuse under § 843.5(A).

issues.label: Sufficiency of evidence for child neglect convictions
issues.why: Rule 29 requires assessing whether evidence supports each element of neglect under § 843.5(C).

issues.label: Assimilation of Oklahoma statute elements
issues.why: Court must ensure the assimilated Oklahoma offense elements were properly applied to Mrs. Smith.
